svg.title: Energy changes
svg.desc: Exothermic vs endothermic: Exothermic: energy to surroundings; temperature rises; products lower in energy. Combustion, many oxidations, neutralisation. Endothermic: energy from surroundings; temperature falls; products higher. Thermal decomposition is an example. Reaction profiles: Vertical axis: energy. Horizontal: reaction progress, not time. Activation energy = minimum energy for a successful collision. Draw a curved peak. Activation energy: reactant level → peak. Overall change: reactant → product level. Bonds: break minus make: Breaking bonds takes energy; forming bonds releases energy. Overall = total broken − total formed. Negative → exothermic; positive → endothermic. Count every bond and equation coefficient; use supplied values. Temperature practical: Insulated cup/lid, measured volumes, same starting temperature. Mix/stir; record maximum/minimum. Change = extreme − initial. Vary one factor; control others, repeat and average. Heat loss can reduce measured rise; use time-graph extrapolation when requested. Cells & batteries: Different electrodes + electrolyte → electricity. Voltage depends on both; compare under controlled conditions. Non-rechargeable stops when a reactant runs out. External current reverses reactions in rechargeable cells. Series cell voltages add. Hydrogen fuel cells: Continuous H₂ and O₂ supply; hydrogen oxidised, oxygen reduced. Overall: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Electrons go through external load; ions through electrolyte. Compare refuelling/recharging, storage, cost, lifetime and whole-process emissions, not only water at the outlet.
